children: said on Monday it would contribute $250 million over the coming years to a fund aimed at addressing environmental and human rights impacts linked to the former Panguna copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea's Bougainville region.
The fund will be established jointly with the Autonomous Bougainville Government (ABG) and ASX-listed Bougainville Copper
(BCL) following consultations with community leaders, the miner said in a statement.

In 2024, a report titled 'Panguna Mine Legacy Impact Assessment (PMLIA)' found that Rio Tinto's mine in Bougainville posed several life-threatening risks, including but not limited to unstable buildings and mine-related flooding
Rio Tinto, BCL and ABG sought a roundtable to address the findings of the PMLIA, from which they decided to establish this fund
The total sum will be used to initiate practical responses along the river and delta areas and social programs for communities across all impacted areas, Rio Tinto said
Specific remedy plans are yet to be released, though Rio Tinto said all programs will abide United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs)
Rio Tinto said, projects already underway in the region include the removal of hazardous materials at the former Loloho port, bridge construction, and a multi-year water and sanitation programme
Rio Tinto was formerly the majority shareholder in BCL, the operator of the Panguna mine, before divesting its 53.8% stake in 2016
